message.content: {"12": {"original": "DVDRS is not a pirate network", "rephrased": "The operators of Dvdrs.net assert that their service is not a pirate network, arguing that the accusation of piracy is an insult to their members and that the claim they host illegal files is factually false. They maintain that they provide a legitimate service to copyright holders by offering information rather than hosting content, and they express a strong desire for the Motion Picture Association of America to retract its characterization of them as an organized pirate network to restore their reputation.", "summary": "Dvdrs.net operators deny being a pirate network, claiming they provide a legitimate information service and demand the MPAA retract false accusations."}, "13": {"original": "We are a UK citizen hosting in the US, so US laws don't apply", "rephrased": "The individual behind Dvdrs.net states that as a British citizen currently hosting servers in the United States, they are not subject to US jurisdiction and therefore US laws do not apply to their operations. However, they clarify that this legal distinction does not prevent them from complying with the Motion Picture Association of America if proper communication and legal processes are established, emphasizing a willingness to cooperate once the issue is resolved through dialogue.", "summary": "The Dvdrs.net operator argues that US laws do not apply due to their UK citizenship but remains willing to comply with the MPAA if they engage in proper communication."}, "14": {"original": "We will comply with the MPAA if they communicate", "rephrased": "The administrators of Dvdrs.net condition their compliance with the Motion Picture Association of America on the establishment of direct communication, stating they are prepared to remove specific files if legally instructed. They emphasize that their service has always adhered to local and international laws and express hope that the MPAA will engage with them to resolve the dispute, rather than proceeding with unilateral legal actions that bypass necessary dialogue.", "summary": "Dvdrs.net administrators pledge to comply with the MPAA's demands only if the organization initiates proper communication and legal engagement."}, "15": {"original": "We hope the MPAA retracts their statement and restores our good name", "rephrased": "The leadership of Dvdrs.net explicitly hopes that the Motion Picture Association of America will retract its public statement labeling them as an organized pirate network, arguing that such a claim damages their reputation and misrepresents their actual service. They contend that their platform has never been contacted by legal representatives to remove files and assert that no existing law prohibits the hosting of the specific files in question, urging the MPAA to restore their good name through a fair and communicative legal process.", "summary": "Dvdrs.net leadership urges the MPAA to retract false accusations of piracy to protect their reputation, citing a lack of prior legal contact and the absence of laws banning their specific content."}}
